text:
maya: CI red on main: flaky test in runtime: 'timer_cancellation_race_test'. Failing only on linux-worker-7. Anyone seen this?

ci-bot: build #3421 failed: timer_cancellation_race_test (https://ci.redwood.example/builds/3421). Log excerpt: 'ASSERT: expected canceled==true, got false'

liam: I saw a similar flake last week, could be nondet ordering. Collecting logs + reproducer.

maya: I can kick a rerun, but want to include seed/ENV. Liam, can you bisect or attach repro?

nina: :eyes: tagging @liam since you mentioned a repro.

liam: I'll run local stress with --seed=5463 and the linux CI container image. Might take ~30m.

aaron: If it's timing sensitive, try setting TEST_TIMINGS=1 to capture timestamps in logs. Also suggest adding repeated tries in CI while we bisect.

devops-bot: Queued rerun for build #3421 -> #3422 on linux-worker-7 (requested by maya).

maya: Thanks. Also posting the failing snippet:
```
[2024-11-20T14:33:21Z] ASSERT failed: timer canceled? false
Trace: runtime/clock.cpp:142
```

ci-bot: Rerun #3422 started. Will post status.

liam: Local run with seed=5463 reproduced once, but not consistently. I captured thread dump and will upload to the artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-artifacts/bugs/5463/timer-race.txt

nina: Quick thought: we recently changed the delayed-execution queue to use steady_clock instead of system_clock. Could the granularity differ on that runner?

aaron: Good call. Also check that the mock-time code in tests isn't mixing clocks.

maya: Rerun passed :white_check_mark: but flaky history shows 2/10 failures. Still red in master because latest run failed. We need to triage.

liam: I'll run bisect across combined commits between 6c3a..d8f2 using test harness. ETA 1.5h.

maya: If anyone can spare cycles, please try to reproduce with sanitizers (TSAN) — might surface ordering issue.

aaron: Heads-up: TSAN builds are slower; maybe we do a targeted run on the suspect commit range.

devops-bot: Rerun #3423 (TSAN-targeted) queued.

ci-bot: Rerun #3423 failed. Attaching failing log snippet: 'Timer callback ran after destructor'

nina: That's telling. Could be a race where timer callback is not canceled before object destruction. I'll look at timer lifecycle code.

liam: I suspect the cancel path races with execution path under heavy load. Adding a short handoff epoch counter in the timer struct might help for deterministic cancellation.

maya: For now, let's add temporary CI retry for that test to reduce noise OR mark as flaky with issue link. Which preferred?

aaron: Prefer to triage but short-term mark as flaky to avoid blocking releases. I'll open a PR to add flaky marker with description and link to this thread.

maya: :+1: please attach the failing seeds and logs. liam, nina — coordinate on fix.

liam: Will post bisect result when done. starting now.
